name: Collab
short_description: Partnership-based events that bring together industry sectors and members of the UH and local community.
long_description: Partnerships connect groups with common intersection and bring together industry sectors and the people who steer those sectors in Hawaii. From science, agriculture, and big data to social services and the creative sectors, PACE collaborates with members of the UH and local community. Events are hosted in partnership with organizations that align with PACE's mission. Collaborative initiatives include networking events, leader discussions, and colloquiums focused on specific topics of interest.

name: Entrepreneurship Live
short_description: Speaker series featuring founders and company executives who discuss their entrepreneurial journey with UH students.
long_description: The Entrepreneurship Live speaker series invites founders and company executives to discuss their entrepreneurial journey with University of Hawai'i students. Each event features individuals who educate and inspire students by sharing their real-world challenges and triumphs, and the range of emotional experiences in forging a startup. Each talk is followed by Q&A and a networking session. The networking session gives the chance for students from various disciplines to interact with each other and with the presenter. The series is free and open to all UH students.
eligibility: Free and open to all UH students.

name: Level Up Workshop
short_description: Workshops on various topics relevant to student entrepreneurs, featuring community members with industry expertise.
long_description: PACE hosts Level Up Workshops on various topics of interest that are relevant to student entrepreneurs. Each event features a member of the community who has expertise in a specific industry. Level Up Workshops offer the opportunity for students to learn together and meet new people in a safe environment. Events are free and open to all UH System students and faculty.
eligibility: Free and open to all UH System students and faculty.

name: Liftoff Advisors
short_description: Program designed to support venture founders in the period after founding but prior to revenue generation.
long_description: Liftoff Advisors (LA) is a program designed to support venture founders in the delicate period after venture founding, but prior to revenue generation. LA offers expert professional advisory services to select UH ventures with the aim of enabling investor-readiness. LA is a milestone-based program wherein participants meet monthly with a handpicked set of advisors and PACE staff. The goal of Liftoff Advisors is to build market-ready, investor-ready ventures that are positioned for sustainability. Selected UH ventures are paired with an interdisciplinary group of talented and experienced professionals.

name: Maker Program
short_description: Maker spaces and recording studio at the Walter Dods, Jr. RISE Center for exploring, experimenting, and bringing ideas to life.
long_description: Explore, experiment and bring your ideas to life in PACE's maker spaces and recording studio at the Walter Dods, Jr. RISE Center. The creative spaces and programs are managed by a group of dedicated UH students. Programs and services are open to all UH System students. Prior experience is not required.
eligibility: Open to all UH System students. Prior experience is not required.

name: Mixers
short_description: Events for student entrepreneurs to learn and connect across different majors.
long_description: PACE presents Mixers to give fellow student entrepreneurs a chance to learn and connect. PACE welcomes participation from students across different majors to learn together and build a community. Each session is a chance for students to exchange ideas and meet others in a relaxed setting. It's an open invitation for all UH System students and faculty to join in for free.
eligibility: Open to all UH System students and faculty. Free.

name: PACE Leaders
short_description: Community of student leaders who lead programs, manage events, and support PACE initiatives across the UH system, with scholarship opportunities.
long_description: PACE Leaders is a leadership and scholarship opportunity for UH students who want hands-on experience supporting real programs, events, and initiatives at PACE. Open to all majors on all 10 UH System campuses. Benefits include hands-on experience leading programs and managing events; access to tools, maker spaces, and resources at the 10,000-square-foot innovation center; network building with industry leaders, entrepreneurs, and peers; professional development opportunities including invitations to community events and conferences; and exclusive scholarship funds (with the largest scholarship pool reserved for students living at the Walter Dods, Jr. RISE Center). No prior experience in entrepreneurship or business is required.
eligibility: Open to all majors on all 10 UH System campuses. No experience in entrepreneurship or business is required.

name: Summer Startup Launchpad
short_description: Free 6-week intensive program providing education and mentorship to help student entrepreneurs test ideas through customer discovery and minimum viable products.
long_description: Summer Startup Launchpad is a free, 6-week intensive program that provides education and mentorship to help student entrepreneurs test their ideas through customer discovery and building minimum viable products. The program teaches entrepreneurship based on a lean methodology of building a startup, providing an experiential, hands-on learning environment with supplemental mentorship from community experts. Participants commit to a minimum of 30 hours per week, with mandatory in-person meeting days twice a week at UH Manoa. Participants may receive monetary awards dependent on the program's budget and individual performance; only current and classified UH students may receive funding.
eligibility: Individuals or teams of 2-4 people. At least one team member must be a classified UH student enrolled in a degree-seeking program with a valid UH ID. All entries must be for new ideas or existing companies less than one year old.

name: Professional-in-Residence
short_description: Connects UH students and faculty with local business professionals through office hours on the UH Manoa campus.
long_description: The Professional-in-Residence (PIR) program connects UH students and faculty with local business professionals. PACE hosts volunteer mentors each semester with varying professional experiences and deep knowledge in their areas of expertise. PIRs rotate each week and hold office hours on the UH Manoa campus. PIRs have expertise in one or more of the following areas: business, entrepreneurship, law, intellectual property, marketing, finance, or venture funding. They offer practical knowledge and advice on specific entrepreneurial issues. Appointments are required, and PIRs donate their time and knowledge without compensation.

name: Virtual Professional-in-Residence
short_description: Connects UH students and faculty with business professionals via e-mail and phone.
long_description: The Virtual Professional-in-Residence (VPIR) program connects UH students and faculty with business professionals by way of e-mail and phone. Beyond classroom education, students may receive leads to job opportunities and valuable insight about specific industries. VPIRs offer practical knowledge and advice, and may introduce faculty and students to colleagues for further assistance. VPIRs have expertise in entrepreneurship, law, intellectual property, marketing, finance, or venture funding. VPIRs are full-time business professionals volunteering their time and expertise; appointments must be scheduled in advance.
eligibility: Current University of Hawaii students and faculty.

name: Entrepreneurs-in-Residence
short_description: In-house mentors who provide new venture mentorship, guidance, and expertise to individuals or startups.
long_description: PACE hosts in-house Entrepreneurs-in-Residence (EIRs) who provide new venture mentorship, guidance, and expertise to individuals or startups. Key responsibilities include: mentorship (offering guidance and sharing insights from their own experiences); pitch coaching (constructive feedback on presentations); strategic advice on business development, market positioning, and growth strategies; networking (connecting entrepreneurs with valuable contacts, partners, and investors); problem solving; innovation (introducing new ideas and best practices); and incubation (hands-on support for startups, potentially including temporary operational roles).

name: 3D Wealth and Financial Literacy Program
short_description: Empowers UH students to build a brighter financial future through tools, resources, and one-on-one mentorship.
long_description: The 3D Wealth & Financial Literacy Program at the University of Hawai'i helps students develop the knowledge, skills, and confidence to take control of their financial futures. Offerings include free access to online tools (budget worksheets, credit score estimators, educational modules), one-on-one financial support from a Financial Wellness Mentor located on the second floor of the Walter Dods, Jr. RISE Center, and resources for job hunting and career exploration. The program offers regular office hours Tuesday through Friday with both in-person and Zoom availability.

name: External Competitions
short_description: PACE sponsors teams of UH students to participate in national and international showcases and competitions.
long_description: PACE sponsors teams of students to participate in national and international showcases and competitions. Teams receive guidance and mentorship in preparation for their appearance. It is important for the University of Hawaii to be represented at these highly visible events, and equally important for participants to gain invaluable experiences and insights from competing alongside students from top universities.

name: Innovate 808
short_description: Weekend business competition where students work directly with founders and CEOs of partner companies, with cash awards for winning teams.
long_description: Innovate 808 is a weekend business competition where students work directly with the founders and CEOs of partner companies, and winning teams win cash awards. The competition is held over 2 Saturdays. Real-world companies present their problem and students pitch their solution. Students may participate as a team or individual. Cash award amounts are decided by the company sponsor and PACE; awards are taxable. Spring 2026 partnered with Meadow Gold Dairies Hawaii. Only currently enrolled UH students may receive awards.

name: PACE Kick Off
short_description: Pitch event where UH students and faculty present startup ideas to a live audience that votes for the grand prize winner.
long_description: PACE welcomes UH entrepreneurs to present their startup idea at a pitch event. Participants must be a current, classified UH student or UH faculty. Participants have 1 minute to pitch and convince the live audience to support their business idea (slides not allowed; visual aids and props permitted). After the pitching round, spectators vote for their favorite idea, with the highest-voted idea crowned MVP and winning the grand prize. Spectators can also participate in a social media challenge for a second grand prize. The event is free, but participants must pre-register to be eligible for prizes.
eligibility: Current, classified UH student or UH faculty.

name: UH Venture Competition
short_description: Semester-long competition providing hands-on education, mentorship, and resources to UH students seeking to start a new business.
long_description: The UH Venture Competition (UHVC) provides hands-on education, mentorship, and resources to University of Hawai'i students who seek to start a new business. Open to students from all 10 UH System campuses. Launching in 2000 (formerly the UH Business Plan Competition), the UHVC has grown into one of the most exciting feature events of the UH entrepreneurial ecosystem. The competition is intense and semester-long, encouraging collaboration across disciplines including Engineering, Computer Science, Medicine, Art, Molecular Biosciences and Bioengineering, Tropical Agriculture, and Business. The competition consists of three rounds over the spring semester: Slide Deck and Business Summary, Semifinal, and Final Round. PACE hosts a series of workshops in conjunction with the competition. Cash prizes include a $10,000 first place (sponsored by Hawaiian Electric and HEI), $5,000 second place, and $2,500 third place (sponsored by HiBEAM), plus in-kind awards from sponsors including marketing consultation, go-to-market strategy services, and incorporation packages.
eligibility: University of Hawai'i students from any of the 10 UH System campuses.

name: Calvin Shindo Student Venture Fund
short_description: Student-run venture capital fund offering pre-seed investments to early-stage UH-affiliated companies.
long_description: The Calvin Shindo Student Venture Fund is a student-run venture capital fund providing pre-seed investments to students and alumni from all 10 UH System community colleges and universities. Managed by a diverse group of UH students. The fund has a total of $125,000 in available funding, with individual investments of up to $5,000 per venture, and up to $25,000 awarded per year. Investments are made in exchange for equity, subject to UH Foundation regulations. The investment process is overseen by a Fund Board composed of experienced investors. The program is made possible by the gift of Dustin Shindo and named in honor of his father, Calvin. Any investment returns are reinvested in the fund.
eligibility: Full-time or part-time, undergraduate or graduate UH students enrolled in a degree-seeking program at any of the 10 UH System community colleges and universities; UH alumni within 5 years of graduation; or student or faculty licensees of UH technology. UH faculty-run ventures are also eligible if their student and alumni team members meet the criteria.

name: Interdisciplinary Research Teams
short_description: PACE supports interdisciplinary studies in which students from different academic backgrounds collaborate to explore new ventures.
long_description: PACE believes that the most successful startups are born from collaboration between disciplines—science, engineering, law, and business working together to come up with viable recommendations and solutions. PACE supports and encourages interdisciplinary studies, in which students from different academic backgrounds explore new ventures. Past projects include Coral Cryopreservation (in collaboration with the Hawaii Institute for Marine Biology and the University of Minnesota, exploring commercial potential for a cryo freezing device) and the Hawaii Grown Tea Study (in collaboration with the College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources, researching the feasibility of large-scale tea farming and production in Hawai'i).

name: Kalo Grants
short_description: Small grants of $500 and $1,000 to UH students of any major who wish to develop and grow new ventures.
long_description: The Kalo Grants program provides small amounts of funding to students who wish to develop new ventures, with the program named after the kalo (taro) plant that is integral to Hawaiian culture. Open to all majors. The program offers $500 grants and $1,000 grants. Goals include giving students opportunity and encouragement to pursue and develop ideas, supporting lifestyle ideas that benefit from small seed funding, developing skills required of new founders, and spurring innovation and entrepreneurial activity at UH. Applicants for the $500 grant do not give a pitch; $1,000 finalists are required to participate in pitch coaching and present at a live event, where awardees are selected via live audience vote. Recipients can ladder from $500 to $1,000 for the same idea, but $1,000 recipients are not eligible to apply for $500 grants for the same idea.
eligibility: Individuals or teams of up to 5 people, including at least one current student enrolled in a degree-seeking program at any of the 10 UH campuses. UH students must lead. Open to all majors. Entries must be for new ideas; businesses operating more than 1 year and previous award-winning ideas (e.g., UH Venture Competition, PACE Entrepreneurs, Kalo Grants) are ineligible.

name: PACE Entrepreneurs
short_description: Cohort program for students focused on building and launching a new venture, with mentorship, resources, and seed funding.
long_description: PACE Entrepreneurs is a cohort of students focused on building and launching a new venture. The program supports promising entrepreneurs who are actively building their product, service, or company. Benefits include customized mentorship, working alongside other student founders, special invitations to PACE and entrepreneurial community events, invitations to industry meetings and conferences (including Hawaii Angels and East Meets West), special access to PACE's network of business professionals, entrepreneurs, attorneys, and investors, showcasing at PACE and Shidler College of Business events, achievement awards for top performers, seed funding to assist with startup expenses, and the opportunity to represent UH at competitions and exhibitor shows outside Hawai'i. The Summer 2026 cohort runs May 26 through July 16, with mandatory in-person meetings twice a week at the Walter Dods Jr. RISE Center on UH Manoa campus. Student founders are invited by PACE Staff to participate.
eligibility: Current, classified University of Hawaii students from any UH campus, with a creative perspective and passion for entrepreneurship and a desire to start their own business or contribute to a startup team.

name: PACE Faculty Fellows
short_description: Recognizes and supports UH faculty making significant contributions to entrepreneurship education across any discipline or campus.
long_description: The PACE Faculty Fellows program recognizes and supports faculty who are making significant contributions to entrepreneurship education at the University of Hawaii. Faculty from any discipline and any campus, who are integrating core entrepreneurial concepts into their teaching, are invited to participate. PACE supports faculty participants in the EL3vate program, a faculty professional development initiative aimed at incorporating experiential learning, entrepreneurial frameworks, and engineering design thinking into course curricula. EL3vate was developed in collaboration with the UH Online Innovation Center.
eligibility: UH faculty from any discipline and any campus who are integrating core entrepreneurial concepts into their teaching.

name: PACE Scholarships
short_description: Multiple scholarship opportunities for UH students, including RISE Center housing scholarships, the RISE Innovation Scholars Program, and the James P.D. Thropp Scholarship.
long_description: PACE offers several scholarship opportunities thanks to donors and partners. The Walter Dods, Jr. RISE Center Housing Scholarship provides up to $6,000 (or $500 per month) toward residency at the RISE Center for UH students (undergraduate or graduate) who participate in or are interested in joining PACE; recipients must maintain a minimum 3.0 GPA, enroll in at least 12 credit hours per semester, and attend PACE events. The RISE Innovation Scholars Program provides a $5,000 scholarship plus mentorship from PACE Entrepreneur- and Professionals-in-Residence, access to the Kīpuka coworking space, networking with investors and founders, and skill development through workshops and maker spaces. The James P.D. Thropp Scholarship for the Shidler-RISE Program provides a $5,000 scholarship for Shidler College of Business students living at RISE; recipients must complete service to community/school activities each semester and attend at least three PACE activities. PACE Leaders is a separate leadership and scholarship opportunity for UH students supporting PACE programs and events.
eligibility: UH students participating in or interested in PACE; specific eligibility (campus, GPA, residency at RISE, Shidler enrollment, etc.) varies by individual scholarship.
